title: CAP & PACELC Consistency-Latency Trade-Offs
prompt: A global e-commerce service runs on a 3-region Raft cluster (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1; RTTs: US-EU 75 ms, EU-IN 130 ms, US-IN 195 ms) with 60,000 RPS catalog reads (95%) and 3,000 RPS ledger writes (5%). Default PC/EC linearizable reads and writes push ap-south-1 checkout p99 past 390 ms and catalog reads past 150 ms (SLA < 120 ms). Redesign using PACELC.

spark.summary: Even with zero network partitions, PC/EC multi-region Raft clusters pay cross-continent quorum and leaseholder RTTs on every read and write, blowing past tail-latency SLAs.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, apply PACELC per workload: keep monetary/inventory writes PC/EC on regional leaseholders, and serve 95% catalog reads PA/EL via local follower reads (`AS OF SYSTEM TIME '-5s'`) with HLC session tokens for read-your-own-writes.

explanation.core:

decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.

decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Workload-Split PACELC + Bounded Staleness

explanation.core:
- **Catalog Reads (`95%` = `57,000 RPS`, `PA/EL`)**: Serve from local regional replicas with bounded staleness (`AS OF SYSTEM TIME '-5s'`), cutting latency from `195 ms` to `< 4 ms` and open connections from `11,700` to `228`.
- **Geo-Partitioned Writes (`5%` = `3,000 RPS`, `PC/EC`)**: Home user/order Raft ranges to the user's region (5-replica Raft: 3 in home region for `< 8 ms` local quorum, 2 remote for DR) while keeping global inventory/wallet writes strongly consistent.
- **Read-Your-Own-Writes Guard**: Attach an HLC session cookie (`last_write_hlc`) for `5 s` after a mutation to route that user's reads to the leaseholder.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of CAP & PACELC Consistency-Latency Trade-Offs, watch how enterprise solution: workload-split pacelc + bounded staleness interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Even with zero network partitions, PC/EC multi-region Raft clusters pay cross-continent quorum and leaseholder RTTs on every read and write, blowing past tail-latency SLAs.

options.text: Record the mutation's HLC timestamp in a short-lived session cookie/header and route that user's reads to the leaseholder for the 5-second staleness window

options.text: Disable Hybrid Logical Clocks so followers always serve the highest local timestamp regardless of commit status
options.feedback: Disabling HLC breaks causal snapshot consistency across replicas.

options.text: Force every catalog read to acquire a 3-continent Raft quorum
options.feedback: Quorum reads reintroduce the 195 ms+ speed-of-light penalty on all 57,000 RPS.
